root.name: Ponziani Opening: Spanish Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. c3 d5 4. Bb5

overview: Against the Ponziani, Black plays 3...d5 and White pins the knight with 4.Bb5. The main branch continues 4...dxe4 5.Nxe5 Qd5 6.Qa4 (the Nikitin Gambit), where Black has the extra e-pawn for a moment and White gets a lead in development and pressure on c6. Play is sharp and open, and Black has to know the tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Pin the knight with Bb5 and take back on e5 with Nxe5
Use Qa4 to threaten the Nc6 and develop quickly

black_ideas.idea: Win the e-pawn and defend with ...Qd5 and ...Bd7
Return material at the right time and simplify

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the e-file and early queen moves
Pinned Nc6 against a White queen on a4

character.notes: Early queen moves and tactics against the pinned knight make the game forcing for both sides.

gambit.notes: After 5.Nxe5 the e-pawn is regained, so material is level and no gambit is on the board.

soundness.notes: Playable for both sides; White does not gain a clear edge.

structure.notes: The e-file opens early and pieces fight for central squares.

approach.notes: The Ponziani is seldom chosen by strong players, and this branch even less.

level.notes: The forcing lines must be known.
